entry.title: Practical, Round-Optimal Lattice-Based Blind Signatures. Blind signatures are a fundamental cryptographic primitive with numerous practical applications.
entry.summary:
Blind signatures are a fundamental cryptographic primitive with numerous practical applications. While there exist many practical blind signatures from number-theoretic assumptions, the situation is far less satisfactory from post-quantum assumptions. In this work, we provide the first overall practical, lattice-based blind signature, supporting an unbounded number of signature queries and additionally enjoying optimal round complexity.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: TLShare: Private Authenticated MPC and FHE Inputs Over TLS. Transport Layer Security (TLS) is the backbone of the web, allowing clients to establish secure and private channels with servers.
entry.summary:
Transport Layer Security (TLS) is the backbone of the web, allowing clients to establish secure and private channels with servers. DECO (CCS'20) and follow-up works proposed protocols that enable proving the provenance of a TLS response, i.e., that a payload came from a particular server, without needing server-side modifications. Unfortunately, these works are limited to proving Boolean statements over the payload (e.g., age $\ge$ 18) and cannot combine payloads from multiple clients.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Efficient (Functional) Bootstrapping for CKKS over the Conjugate-Invariant Ring
entry.summary:
The CKKS fully homomorphic encryption scheme enables efficient encrypted computation over complex-valued data. In many real-world cases, however, the computation only involves real data, and storing them inside complex slots wastes the encoding ability. This motivated the design of conjugate-invariant CKKS (CI-CKKS) instantiated over the conjugate-invariant ring (CIR), which provides the same number of real slots while halving the RLWE dimension.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: On Lifting AGM Security to the AGM with Oblivious Sampling. The Algebraic Group Model (AGM) is widely used to prove the security of cryptographic schemes involving groups and pairings.
entry.summary:
The Algebraic Group Model (AGM) is widely used to prove the security of cryptographic schemes involving groups and pairings. It requires adversaries to explain how their output group elements are obtained from the elements they have received. The AGM with Oblivious Sampling (AGMOS), introduced by Lipmaa, Parisella, and Siim (TCC 2023), additionally allows adversaries to sample group elements without learning their discrete logarithms.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #logic #combinatorics

entry.title: Towards Formal Security Proofs of MQOM
entry.summary:
Recent MPC-in-the-Head (MPCitH) signatures increasingly rely on aggressive GGM-tree optimizations to reduce signature size and computational cost, culminating in __secret-key-root correlated GGM trees__ as used in SBC (Huth and Joux, CRYPTO 2024), MQOM (NIST PQC Standardization for Additional Signature Round-2, 2024), and rBN++ (Kim, Lee, and Son, EUROCRYPT 2025). While this technique yields substantial compression, it introduces a dependency loop in the proof (Kosuge and Xagawa, CiC 2026(3)). We analyze MQOM and resolve this circularity by providing EUF-CMA security proofs for a slightly modified variant.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
